title: Entropy and Information
oneLine: Measure how much uncertainty a distribution carries, in bits.

paras: Entropy quantifies surprise. A fair coin is maximally uncertain (1 bit); a loaded one carries less. It is the currency behind decision-tree splits (which question removes the most uncertainty?), cross-entropy loss, and compression.
Entropy is the expected number of bits to encode an outcome:
sections.texNote: Maximized by the uniform distribution; zero when one outcome is certain.

sections.caption: A decision tree picks the split that drops this the most.

takeaways: Information gain (entropy drop) drives decision-tree splits.
Cross-entropy, the workhorse classification loss, is built from it.
